title: PowerPoint on the web: Copilot agent notifies you when work is complete or needs attention
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts and existing licence controls are supported, and its feature-specific documentation gaps survived targeted searches. One descriptive statement goes beyond the evidence: Microsoft has not specified that notifications appear outside the PowerPoint tab.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: User licences are managed in Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section

claims.claim: The documented Microsoft Graph PowerShell call assigns a user licence using Set-MgUserLicense with UserId, AddLicenses.SkuId and an empty RemoveLicenses array.
claims.quote: To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell. Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Copilot > Settings is the documented Microsoft 365 admin center page to review Copilot settings.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, expand Copilot, and then select Settings.

claims.claim: The Copilot settings documentation lists User access, Data access, Copilot actions and Other settings, without a setting concerning these notifications.
claims.quote: Browse User access, Data access, Copilot actions, and Other settings. Select View all or All settings when a setting isn't shown in a category.
